title: Hojaldre de Mantequilla (Puff Pastry with Butter)
description: A pastry dish made with butter, egg white, and flour.

ingredients.name: about half an ounce of fine salt

ingredients.name: as much butter as one egg

ingredients.name: half a pound of butter for layering
ingredients.sourceText: half a pound of butter for layering

steps: Pile {{source-0}} on a table and make a hollow in the middle
Add about half an ounce of fine salt, one egg white, one good glass of water, and as much butter as one egg
Mix everything together by hand, kneading it lightly and being careful that no lumps form
The dough should be neither very hard nor very soft, and knead as quickly as possible so it does not heat up from the warmth of the hands
After a quarter hour, flatten the dough slightly with a rolling pin or stick, placing half a pound of butter on top and flattening it as well
Fold the two ends of the dough, folding one over the other so that the butter is enclosed in the interior, and let rest for half an hour
Give it two turns, let twenty minutes pass, and then give it two more turns
Form the pastries and place them in the oven to bake, or use the dough for pastries or whatever is needed

title: Huevos en el Platón (Eggs in the Platter)
description: Prepared with eggs, butter, and salt.
steps: Cover the bottom of a platter that can withstand the action of fire with butter.
Sprinkle a little salt on it and break the fresh eggs in the platter, making sure the yolks remain whole.
Then sprinkle with fine salt mixed with pepper, placing a small ball of butter on top of each egg, and the platter over hot ashes.
Sometimes the eggs cook too much underneath and remain raw on top, but this inconvenience is avoided by passing over the eggs a spatula heated in the fire.
It is necessary to keep the spatula at a certain distance so that the yolks cook without hardening. This way of cooking eggs is more elegant than the ordinary way.

Plug all holes and cook the eggs in hot water without letting them boil.

Serve as an intermediate course on a folded napkin.

steps: Cover a wild boar leg on all sides with fat ham

Place it in a pot of the same size with some slices of ham, sliced onions, carrot skins, large turnips, a good bunch of parsley and small onions, two garlic heads, four cloves of spice, two laurel leaves, thyme, basil, salt and coarse pepper
Let it sweat for half an hour over gentle fire
Moisten with half cuartillo of refined Spanish brandy, two cuartillos of white wine and broth
Make it sweat again over gentle fire for six or seven hours
Let the leg cool in its own cooking liquid
Serve as a grand cold dish with its sauce, which should be light and of good taste

Pour the jelly into small jars or cups placed on snow or in a cool place

steps: Cook whatever quantity of texocotes you wish without peeling, and after they are cooked, peel them, dry them and give them a boil in clean water, then leave them in the same water for twenty-four hours so they release the phlegm.

Make clarified syrup in the proportion of one pound of sugar for each cuartillo and a half of the phlegmy water of the texocotes, and with the syrup at point, mix both things and put them to boil until they have the necessary degree of cooking, which is known by taking with the spoon a little of the syrup and throwing it in cold water, from where it will be taken by grasping with the fingers, between which it should make small threads.
In this case remove the syrup from the heat, and carefully remove all the foam that forms when the bubbles rise to the surface of the pot.
Once the jelly is well skimmed, empty it into the plates or molds, which will be placed uncovered in the sun so they form a crust.
You can mix with the jelly to give it novelty, some grains of uva, and the same can be done with the other fruits.

title: Jaletina (Orange Aspic Jelly)
description: Prepared with orange, veal, and oranges.
steps: Cook three well-cleaned veal feet in sufficient water until they fall apart
Remove the fat from the broth by passing it through a sieve
Measure eight cuartillos and strain through new linen as many times as necessary to remove all fat

Place on heat until it boils vigorously
Pour into a flannel bag to distill

title: Jaletina a la Francesa (French Aspic)
description: Prepared with aspic, lemon, and egg whites.

ingredients.name: Cow feet (as many as desired for the amount of aspic to be made)
ingredients.sourceText: Cow feet (as many as desired for the amount of aspic to be made)

ingredients.name: One good rooster, plucked, singed over flame, and cleaned
ingredients.sourceText: One good rooster, plucked, singed over flame, and cleaned

ingredients.name: Two or three lemon peels, cleaned of white pith
ingredients.sourceText: Two or three lemon peels, cleaned of white pith

ingredients.name: Juice of the lemons whose peels were used
ingredients.sourceText: Juice of the lemons whose peels were used

steps: Prepare the cow feet by washing and cleaning them thoroughly
Pluck, singe over flame, and clean the rooster
Place both the cow feet and rooster in a pot with sufficient water
Bring to a boil and skim carefully and thoroughly
When the meats are completely broken down, the aspic is at the right point, without needing to be overly strong
Strain through fine cloth or linen and remove the fat thoroughly
Add sugar in proportion, cinnamon sticks, two or three cloves, and two or three cleaned lemon peels
Allow the aspic to cook for some time with these ingredients
In the meantime, beat four or five egg whites until they harden
Mix the juice of the lemons into the beaten egg whites
Add this mixture to the aspic, stirring it occasionally over the heat
Allow it to come to a boil until it rises, approaching the point of overflowing from the edges
Filter through fine cloth or felt until it is very clear
Place in a cold location to set
Optional: color the aspic using cochineal or kermes for red, beet juice for crimson, tournesol dye for violet, egg yolks for yellow, cooked chard or spinach for green, or almond milk for white

title: Jaletina de Vino (Wine Aspic Jelly)
description: Prepared with wine, veal, and oranges.
steps: Cook three veal feet until they fall apart completely; strain the broth
Measure eight cuartillos and remove the fat by straining through a damp napkin with hot broth

Place one pound and nine ounces of sugar, two sweet oranges with peel cut into pieces and one peeled, a little cinnamon in sticks, half a cuartillo of brandy, half of muscatel wine, and four eggs with shell
Place the pot on active heat without flame, because the brandy will ignite; when it comes to a boil, add the broth to boil quickly

To remove from the mold, place it in hot water for a moment and turn it over

title: Jaletina Listada (Striped Aspic)
description: Prepared with cream, egg yolks, and isinglass.

ingredients.name: One and a half ounces of isinglass dissolved
ingredients.sourceText: One and a half ounces of isinglass dissolved

ingredients.name: Spinach green (see green officinal of spinach, page 322) with some crushed bitter macaroons
ingredients.sourceText: Spinach green (see green officinal of spinach, page 322) with some crushed bitter macaroons

steps: Cook two quarts of cream
Pour into a saucepan and dissolve nine egg yolks in it
Add a little salt and half a pound of sugar
Place the saucepan over very gentle heat, avoiding boiling, and stir until it thickens
Pass through fine cloth or a silk sieve
Add one and a half ounces of dissolved isinglass
Divide this composition into four equal parts, pouring each into a separate glass
To one part add orange blossom
To another add spinach green with some crushed bitter macaroons
In the third add blanc mange
In the last add a chocolate infusion
Pour the first infusion onto the mold on the ice to the thickness of a finger
When it has set, pour the second in the same amount
Continue in this manner until the mold is full
Sprinkle salt on the ice
At the moment of serving, unmold the aspic

description: Prepared with ham, red wine, and carrots.
steps: Trim the ham to remove any bad parts, without removing the skin or crust
Leave it three days in water to desalt, increasing or decreasing the time depending on whether it is new or old and how much salt it has
Wrap it in clean cotton cloth and place it in a pot or marmite of its size
Add six quartillos of water and the same amount of red wine with carrots, turnips, onions and a good bunch of assorted fine herbs
Let the ham cook for five or six hours over moderate fire
When cooked, let it cool in its own broth, then remove it and gently remove the covering without separating the fat
Place chopped parsley with a bit of pepper on top
Cover with bread crumbs and pass a shovel heated to coals over it so the crumbs absorb some fat and take on a beautiful color
Serve cold on a napkin as a thick course

title: Kirschwasser (Cherry Brandy)
description: Prepared with cherries.
steps: Remove the stems from ripe black cherries
Fill a medium barrel with them
Cover with wet ash or thick mortar to form a crust that maintains the spirituous essence of the fruit in fermentation and prevents it from evaporating
After one month or six weeks, remove the covering and prepare the remaining cherries for distillation
Place the grate in the cucurbit, fill it to two-thirds with the juice and pulp of the cherries
Assemble the still and conduct the fire with caution and gradually until only a thin stream drips
Obtain a very clear liquor, ceasing the operation as soon as you perceive that the tails (weak flavorless product) begin to pass
Discard the refuse from the first product and place the same quantity of cherries as the first time back in the cucurbit, continuing until everything is distilled
Rectify the kirschwasser afterward in a bain-marie, which should reach twenty-two to twenty-three degrees after this second distillation

title: Lamb Trotters with Light Sauce (Manitas de Carnero a la Salsa Ligada)
description: Prepared with lamb, broth, and sauce.
steps: Cook the lamb trotters in light white broth for four hours
Test for doneness by pressing with fingers until meat yields easily and feels tender
Remove and drain the trotters, trim the extremities so the feet remain whole and clean
Place in a saucepan and add six ladle-fulls of curled sauce and four of concentrated broth
Allow to reduce until only half remains
Just before serving, add a liaison of two egg yolks with a little nutmeg to the sauce
Once thickened, strain the sauce and pour over the trotters, which should be kept hot but not boiling
Add some black pepper

If curled sauce is not available, prepare an alternative broth: in a saucepan with butter, add finely minced garlic and parsley, cook until rendered, add one spoonful of flour with salt, black pepper, nutmeg and broth, bring to boil, thicken with egg yolks, and finish with lemon juice at service

title: Leche Quemada (Burned Milk)
description: Prepared with milk, egg yolks, and sugar.
steps: Bring two quartillos of milk to boil with cinnamon sticks and sweeten to taste
Set aside about one large cup and dissolve a little syrup in it, then mix with the rest
Allow to cool, then return to heat until it thickens
Remove from heat and let cool completely
Mix in several egg yolks that have been broken but not beaten, to give a good yellow color
Return to fire until it thickens enough to form a skin
When very cold, cover the milk well with finely ground sugar
Burn the top with a hot iron blade

title: Leche Quemada (Burnt Milk Custard)
description: Prepared with milk, starch, and egg yolks.

ingredients.name: ground and sifted starch
ingredients.sourceText: one cup of ground and sifted starch

steps: Mix the ground and sifted starch with the eight quartillos of milk
Divide the entire mixture into two halves
In one half, beat the twelve egg yolks well
Add the other half of the milk and beat everything together
Strain the mixture
Add a small cinnamon stick and a washed lemon zest
Sweeten to taste
Heat to the desired consistency, some preferring it thick enough to cut with a knife, others preferring it looser
Pour into a platter and let cool completely
Sprinkle crushed sugar on top and burn it with a hot iron plate or a red-hot iron paddle
Alternatively, divide the platter into four parts: burn one part as described, cover two others, one with ground cinnamon and another with dragée, leaving the last in its natural color

Stir until the sugar dissolves
Dissolve as many egg yolks as needed for color in the same mixture
Add a handful of ground and sifted starch

title: Lechugas a la Española (Lettuces Spanish Style)
description: Prepared with ham, beef, and carrots.
steps: Parboil the lettuces in salted water, keeping only the most tender parts and washing them well.
Boil for twenty minutes, then cool in cold water.
Squeeze out the water and place a little salt and coarse pepper in the heart of each lettuce.
After tying them, place them in a pot layered with ham slices, some beef slices, two sliced carrots, two onions, two cloves, and one bay leaf.
Cover the lettuces with more ham slices, add broth with a little of the pot liquid, and let them cook slowly for one hour.
When cooked, dry and press with a clean cloth to extract the broth.
Arrange on a plate in the form of a crown with toasted bread slices of similar size, pouring Spanish sauce underneath.

title: Lechugas Picadas (Chopped Lettuces)
description: Prepared with broth, bread, and salt.
steps: Parboil well-washed lettuces in salted water, keeping only the most tender parts.
Remove from hot water and place in fresh water, and when cooled, chop and put in a pan with four ounces of butter, salt and a small amount of pepper.
When the lettuces have fried somewhat, add a small amount of flour proportionate to the lettuces.
Mix everything well, add broth and let boil for a quarter hour.
Arrange on a plate with toasted bread around it and serve.

title: Lechugas Rellenas (Stuffed Lettuces)
description: Prepared with beef, ham, and onions.
steps: Parboil the lettuces for a moment; drain them and open the leaves without removing the stem until reaching the heart.
Remove the heart and in its place put a piece of fine poultry stuffing and tie the lettuces.
Slice two pounds of beef pulp and line a pan with it and with strips of ham and sliced onions.
Let them sweat on the fire and add a little flour.
When it begins to stick, stir it with a spoon on the burner so it browns a little.
Moisten with broth and stock in equal parts, and season with salt, pepper, cloves, bay leaf, basil, parsley and whole onions.
Place the stuffed lettuces in a pot; put the cooked mixture on top, add the broth and let the lettuces cook.

title: Lengua de Carnero a la Gascona (Lamb Tongue Gascony Style)
description: Prepared with lamb, sauce, and onion.
steps: Cut the cooked lamb tongues into strips
In a fire-resistant dish, place a layer of Spanish sauce at the bottom with parsley, onion, half a head of garlic, mushrooms, all chopped very finely, salt and black pepper
Place the tongue strips on top, seasoning them underneath
Cover everything with bread crumbs
Place small pieces of butter the size of a chickpea on top all around, which will nourish the dish and prevent the bread from toasting and turning black from the fire
Place the dish over gentle heat, cover it with the lid of a baking dish, and place fire on top
When the dish is well colored, serve with light sauce

title: Lengua de Ternera a Dos Fuegos (Calf's Tongue on Two Fires)
description: Prepared with tongue, ham, and fat.

ingredients.name: Lean ham, cut into small pieces
ingredients.sourceText: Lean ham, cut into small pieces

steps: Peel the tongue and lard it with small pieces of lean ham
Arrange it in a pot lined with slices of fat ham
Add the onions, carrots, mushrooms, parsley, and bay leaf, seasoned with pepper and salt
Moisten with one glass of broth and one glass of white wine
Cover with more slices of fat ham
Place the pot on gentle heat and put burning coals on the lid or on a comal
After six hours, remove the tongue when cooked
Divide it lengthwise into two parts and serve with a spicy sauce

title: Lengua á la Gendarme (Beef Tongue Gendarme Style)
description: Prepared with beef tongue, broth, and white wine.
steps: Simmer slowly in a casserole one cooked tongue, stripped of its skin and cut into thin slices, with one cup of broth and half a pint of white wine
Season moderately with salt and pepper
When the sauce is sufficiently reduced, remove the tongue slices from the casserole and place on a platter
Add to the sauce a handful of finely chopped parsley, two egg yolks dissolved in a little broth, and a few drops of vinegar
Pour this sauce over the tongue at the moment of serving
